# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 61 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 61 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_061_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 5, Part 7 — Repentance Granted or Withheld

**61:1** "Lord," I said, "is there any hope for people who died before these days of repentance?" "Come with me," he said, "and I'll show you what happens with all those who have doubted and sinned."

**61:2** He showed me a young man sitting in a chair, speaking to a large crowd. "Do you see that young man?" "Yes, lord," I said. "He is the angel of righteousness," he told me. "All those people standing around him are of various kinds. Some are being brought before him; some leave with joy; others leave looking grief-stricken."

**61:3** "And many are just standing and listening. Some who come up to leave go away joyfully; others go away weeping and grieving." "Lord," I said, "I don't understand what I'm seeing." "Let me explain," he said. "The young man in the chair is the angel of righteousness. Those being brought before him are the ones who are going to receive repentance. And let me explain why some leave joyful and others sorrowful."

**61:4** "Those who leave joyfully are those who have taken these words into their hearts and repented with complete sincerity. Repentance has been given to them. Those who leave sorrowfully are people who have turned completely away from God and refuse to repent. Repentance that leads to life is simply not available to them."

**61:5** "What about those who have doubted?" "And those who sinned but never repented?" I asked. "For those who doubted," he said, "repentance is given in proportion to what is in their hearts." Then he said to me: "Don't give the devil a foothold in your heart. He is crafty and devious — very skilled at leading God's servants astray, especially those who are double-minded. So stand firm in your faith and don't give ground."

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity and accessibility, capturing the eschatological repentance vision of Similitude 5.*
